page.layout: One page of verse, one column, centred-indented lines; running head at top centre; page number top left; no margin notes; no catchword or signature. The word "Vanisq;" sits at the lower right as the last printed line of the verse.

main_text.p:
Pauebit altis atque clausa mœnibus
Terrore fracta panico.

Non parcet hostis perfidus cano seni
Non parcet ille paruulis,

Quales benigna blandulos solent sinu
Fouere matres lacteo.

Iuuenta ferro casa corruet truci
Chorique molles virginum.

Iam iam per orbem disiuos sfacidas
Totum volebam spargere.

Nomenque gentis omne prorsus tollere
Qua me repellit impia.

Sed me ferocis hostis impotentia
Mutare visa compulit.

Nam si peremni iuncta mecum fœdere
Proles periret Abrahæ:

Aut subiugata legibus furentium
Seruiret vsque gentium.

Ah! fastuoso verba qua recluderet
Impurus hostis pectore

Hæc solus ipse cuncta feci (diceret)
Potente dextra fortior:

Nunc Gens Isaci viribus meis manus
Tendit subacta supplices

Non præstat ista Ioua vindex quem putat
Decepta Regem Cœlitum
Sed ipsa semet artibus perdit suis

page.notes: Long s rendered as s in one place ("sfacidas") was not converted, since the instructions require a plain s; the printed form is "ssacidas"/"sfacidas" and it is uncertain. Line-initial spacing and the verse lines were reproduced with line breaks inside each stanza paragraph rather than as separate lines; the stanza structure is as printed. The final word "Vanisq;" is set at the right margin and is marked as a line of its own. Faint show-through from the reverse page is present at the right edge and has been omitted. The reading "Iuuenta" and "Chorique" are as printed. Several words are uncertain in the scan and should be checked: "Iam iam" and "disiuos" (possibly "dissiuos").
